title: A pilot and a proof of concept
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Why would he pick a new partner instead of an old one?
Jose asked why a founder with many existing partners would use a brand-new one as the example in his book. He said the answer is that he needs a pilot, a proof of concept.
A student said that it signifies a new partnership and an openness to sharing resources from the beginning.
Another said that it is an easy win but an elevated form of rigor, with a higher perceived value because it is new.
Jose said that forming partnerships is complicated: will the new partner value what you do, and will they have success, as an outsider to the existing group?
What could you use as a pilot that proves your method outside your comfort zone?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the method you want to prove.
Write the new place you could prove it.
Write what a win would look like.
Write what you will do with the proof.
